For each k>=3 and compact [a,b] in (pi,2pi), explicitly constructed x-axis chain plus one point (-s,1) has nearest admissible successor cycle for every alpha in [a,b] by strict angular and metric inequalities. Independently checked all pairwise competitors at 16 varied k/alpha choices (k=3,4,7,20 and apertures near both endpoints); this verifies only finite geometric ingredient. Poisson disjoint positive-probability tile events yield positive density uniformly on compact aperture ranges; spatial ergodic theorem yields almost-sure Palm frequency for fixed aperture, and countable compact exhaustion gives simultaneous positivity. Local stability of each finite orbit plus bounded convergence yields continuity; Campbell-Mecke with Poisson void sectors gives exact (k-1)-tuple Palm integral with no missing factorial. Proof of infinite result rests on these arguments, not finite simulation.
